title: CRLR/23/2015 of Trilok Singh Vs State Of Uttarakhand

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 23 of 2015
Trilok Singh ....Revisionist
Versus
State of Uttarakhand .... Respondent.
Present :
Mr. B.S. Bhandari, Advocate for the revisionist.
Mr. Siddhartha Bisht, Brief Holder for the State of Uttarakhand.

Dated: 29th July, 2019
JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
 The present Criminal Revision has been preferred by one
Mr. Trilok Singh, who was the driver of the Dumper, bearing
registration No. UP-02D-0217. As per the story of prosecution, an
F.I.R. was registered on 8th February, 2005, at about 22.10 by PW6
Suresh, i.e. the complainant, who was son-in-law of the deceased
Samruram, wherein, he has contended that at the place, in question,
i.e. Thana Lal Kuan, District Nainital, when Samruram and other
persons after finishing their day's work, were trying to return back
home, they tried to catch the dumper, in question, and climb the same
from the rear part of the vehicle. It is contended that on 8th February,
2005, when these persons, which included the deceased Samruram,
when they were making their efforts to board the dumper, the
allegation is that the revisionist, Trilok Singh, who was driving the
dumper, without paying any attention towards the activities, which
were being carried out in the rear part of the offending vehicle, i.e.
UP-02D-0217, of the boarding of the person concerned has suddenly
reversed the vehicle as a consequence thereto, the father-in-law of
PW6 Suresh, namely Samruram lost his balance and he fell down and
as a consequence thereto, his legs came under the rear wheel of the
dumper, in question, and he got seriously injured.

2
2. Due to aforesaid accident, which has occurred on
08.02.2005, he has suffered grievous injuries and multiple fractured in
his right thigh and while he was being taken to the hospital, he
succumbed to his injuries on account of excessive blood loss due to
the accident. The post mortem was conducted on the body of
Samruram, who is reported to be of 45 years of age on the date of the
accident. The post mortem report as submitted on 9th February, 2005,
before the Trial Court as an exhibit-2, it has shown that late Samruram
had suffered four grievous injuries on account of the aforesaid
accident, resulting into crushing of his right thigh; multiple abrasion
on part of upper thigh; lacerated wound in the hip on the right side;
multiple abrasion on the back of abdomen on right side as well as
abrasion on the right shoulder of the deceased Samruram.
3. On the basis of the F.I.R., a chargesheet was submitted
and consequent to it, the Criminal Case No. 576 of 2012, was
registered against the present revisionist, who was then driver of the
vehicle with an allegation that on the date of the accident, i.e. 8th
February, 2005, he was driving the dumper, in question, with extreme
negligence, which has resulted into the accident and ultimately the
death of the deceased person.
4. During the course of Trail, number of witnesses were
examined and, particularly, as per the argument which has been
extended by the learned counsel for the revisionist and the statement
recorded of PW6 Suresh, who was the complainant and also one of
the witnesses and son-in-law of the deceased Samruram, had made a
statement to the effect that the cause of the accident was at the behest
of the revisionist on account of his negligence because he has reversed
the vehicle without paying any attention to the activities of persons
boarding the dumper, due to which, deceased Samruram, who wanted
to board the dumper at the relevant point of time, fell down under the
rear wheel of the truck, in question, resulting into his death.

3
5. The learned Trial Court, examined as many as seven
witnesses. PW2 Dr. Neelambar Bhatt, who was produced before the
Trial Court as a Doctor, who had submitted that the cause of death
was on account of the ante mortem injuries and due to extreme blood
loss. Even, if the statement of the complainant PW6 Suresh is
scrutinized, he too, in the manner in which, he has recorded statement
would show that the offence under Sections 279 I.P.C. could not be
said to have been made out to the effect that the vehicle was being
driven rashly and negligently for the reasons that according to the
statement, the allegation levelled against the revisionist was to the
effect that he has reversed the vehicle without paying attention to the
activities, which was being carried out in the rear part of the vehicle,
in question, i.e. of boarding of the persons, who wanted to travel from
the site from where they were working.
6. Reversing of the vehicle at the time when the deceased
was boarding the dumper, this Court is of the view that it would not
fall to be an act of negligent driving, it could be brought to be within
the ambit of human negligence due to lack of diligence with regard to
ensuring the fact that all the passengers, who wanted to travel on the
dumper, in question, had boarded or not and then only the vehicle
could have been started from the place, in question.
7. The learned Trial Court on considering the evidence, had
rendered the judgment on 8th February, 2013, thereby, holding thereof
the revisionist was an accused of commission of offence under
Section 279 I.P.C. to be read with Section 304-A I.P.C. on account of
death of Samruram and, consequently, had inflicted a sentence of
conviction of one month simple imprisonment for commission of an
offence under Section 279 of the I.P.C. and six months simple
imprisonment for commission of an offence under Section 304-A
IPC.

4
8. The said judgment of the learned Trial Court was put to
challenge in an Appeal by the present revisionist before the Additional
Sessions Judge, Haldwani, District Nainital, which was registered as
Criminal Appeal No. 22 of 2013, Trilok Singh Vs. State of
Uttarakhand. The learned Appellate Court too after considering the
propriety of the F.I.R. No. 15/05 and the finding which has been
recorded in the impugned judgment dated 8th February, 2013,
rendered in Criminal Case No. 576 of 2012, State Vs. Trilok Singh
had come to a conclusion that once the revisionist was driving the
vehicle, he owed the responsibility to ensure that the action of
boarding of people on the dumper, in question, ought to have been
completed before the vehicle was put to motion by the revisionist,
hence, held him to be negligent.
9. But, here the said implication would not flow for the
reason that as per the averments of the case as built out by the
complainant, PW6 Suresh, who was son-in-law of the deceased
Samruram, it cannot be said that the act of reversal of vehicle all of a
sudden was deliberate and intentional and hence, it cannot be
attributed that the revisionist was at all responsible for rash and
negligent driving of the offending vehicle, resulting to of rendering of
judgment of conviction for a period of one month simple
imprisonment for the said offence under Section 279 IPC and six
months simple imprisonment for offence under Section 304-A I.P.C.
10. Consequently, it could be said that it was a sheer chance
that at the time when the vehicle was suddenly reversed by the
revisionist, it was the father-in-law of PW6 Suresh, who was at that
point of time boarding the dumper, in question, from rear side, due to
which, he fell down and his leg came under the rear wheel of the
dumper.
11. Having considered the defence, which has been taken and
also the statement of PW2 Dr. Neelambar Bhatt and the post mortem

5
report as placed on record as an exhibit before the Court below, it
cannot be said that as per the set of allegation which has been levelled
against the revisionist could at all be falling to be within the ambit of a
negligent driving as contemplated under Section 279 of the I.P.C. and
consequent thereto, if a sudden happening has chanced resulting into
the death of Samruram, though would constitute to be an offence
under Section 304-A I.P.C. but there was no such animus prevailing in
the minds of the revisionist, which has resulted not the death of late
Samruram.
12. Considering the Lower Court Record and the findings,
which have been recorded by the Courts below, this Court is of the
view that it was a sheer chance and a particular circumstances, which
generated at that point of time suddenly resulting into an accident,
which was not a deliberate or intentional act and, in particular, in the
light of the statement of the oral witnesses, which was adduced by the
parties, it showed that it was because of a human error which has
resulted into the death of Samruram and, hence, it cannot be
nomenclature or classified as to be an offence under Section 279
I.P.C.
13. Consequently, this Court is of the view that the impugned
judgment of conviction as rendered by the Courts below deserves to
be set aside. The judgments of conviction are set aside. The
revisionist is on bail in pursuance to the order dated 23rd January,
2015, he need not to surrender and accordingly the sureties, which
have been advanced for the purposes of availing the bail in pursuance
to the order dated 23rd January, 2015, are directed to be discharged by
the Magistrate concerned.
14. Subject to the above observations, the Revision stands
allowed.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 29.07.2019
Shiv
